subject: Consolidated request: admin event manifests, redaction policy, and delivery checksum
messages:
From: Benjamin Stone <benjamin.stone@helixcare.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: audit@helixcare.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: manifest + redaction guidance + delivery checksum

Hi Sofia,

We've started preparing the SIG/SOC2 evidence bundle for our internal audit and need a couple of clarifications on Redwood's admin-event exports. Specifically: 

1) A manifest format that lists all exported files and their SHA-256 checksums (we need this for chain-of-custody).
2) Preferred export file formats (NDJSON vs Parquet vs CSV) for admin events and whether you include field-level schemas in the manifest.
3) Your redaction policy for PII in admin events (do you provide redacted vs raw, and how are redaction rules recorded?).
4) Delivery methods (S3 presigned URL, SFTP, direct push to our GCS bucket) and whether you provide a signed checksum or PGP-signed manifest.

Can you point me to an example manifest and confirm retention windows applied during the export (we might ask for a timebox snapshot covering 2026-09-01 -> 2026-11-15)?

Thanks,
Ben
Benjamin Stone
Sr. Compliance Manager, HelixCare

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Benjamin Stone <benjamin.stone@helixcare.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: manifest + redaction guidance + delivery checksum

Ben — thanks for the clear list. I can confirm we can produce a timeboxed export for the window you requested. Quick answers up-front:

- Manifest: we include a top-level manifest.json (UTF-8) that lists exported files, per-file sha256, size bytes, exported schema reference (schema_vX.yaml), and a signed_manifest.sig (PGP) when requested.
- Formats: admin events are exported as NDJSON by default (one JSON event per line), with an optional Parquet path for high-volume archives. CSV is available for smaller scoped exports but not recommended for nested fields.
- Redaction: we support two export modes — "redacted" (PII fields replaced with consistent tokens) and "full" (raw). The manifest records which mode was used and includes a redaction_rules.yaml detailing which fields were transformed.
- Delivery: presigned S3 URL (HTTPS) is our standard, but we support encrypted SFTP and direct push to customer GCS buckets with mutual TLS. We attach a sha256sum.txt and can PGP-sign the manifest on request.

I'll attach a manifest template and a small checksum helper script. For the timebox you asked, we need a formal request (one-paragraph PO or an email thread confirmation) to start the export job and get an ETA.

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Manager, Trust & Safety — Redwood Inference

Attachment: logs_manifest_template.json (template)
Attachment: scp-checksum-script.sh (utility)
From: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: manifest + redaction guidance + delivery checksum

Looping in Marcus for data team specifics. A few implementation notes to save us back-and-forth with HelixCare: 

- Event classes we include: admin_console, api_token_creation, api_token_usage, role_changes, key_material_rotation, workspace_deletes, config_audit (feature flags, routing policy changes), and operator_commands.
- Retention policy: hosted API telemetry (aggregated) is 13 months; admin event raw logs are kept 24 months before scheduled irreversible deletion unless an export/hold is requested. For exports, we snapshot the ledger at export time and provide a manifest with a snapshot timestamp.
- Redaction specifics: we tokenize email addresses and IPs in redacted exports using HMAC-SHA256 (with a customer-specific salt when requested). The redaction_rules.yaml enumerates fields and the transform; we do not supply the salt in the manifest.

Marcus — can you confirm the expected size per 30-day window for a medium-sized account (so we can recommend Parquet vs NDJSON)?

-Kim
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: manifest + redaction guidance + delivery checksum

Kim/Team — rough numbers based on current telemetry: medium-sized accounts (50-200 active users, normal activity) generate ~12-18 GB of admin events per 30 days in NDJSON (uncompressed). Parquet (snappy) of the same dataset is typically 20-30% smaller and offers faster columnar filtering for auditors. For HelixCare's three-month window (~Sept 1 - Nov 15), expect ~35-50 GB raw NDJSON.

Operational notes:
- We produce a manifest.json that includes a snapshot_ts and per-file sha256.
- We can produce a signed_manifest.sig (PGP) and a delivery_proof.txt that lists presigned URLs and expiry metadata.
- For chain-of-custody, we recommend they verify sha256(file) == manifest[file].sha256 and that signed_manifest.sig verifies with our Trust key (we provide the public key in the COS - Certificate of Signing).

Lauren — will we need SOC2 team involvement for any manual redaction exceptions?

-Marcus

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Benjamin Stone <benjamin.stone@helixcare.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: manifest + redaction guidance + delivery checksum

Thanks Ben — this all sounds doable. Two operational items from the SOC2 / audit ops side: 

1) Please confirm formally via this thread the exact snapshot window (start/end timestamps in UTC) and whether you want redacted or full exports. Once we have that, we'll open a ticket and give an ETA (typically 3 business days for exports under 100 GB).

2) For any field-level redaction exceptions (e.g., legal/forensic review where they permit access to raw), we'll require a signed Data Access Addendum and an approved request from your security leadership. Please include the approver's name and contact in the request.

Deliverables you should expect:
- manifest.json (includes file list, sizes, sha256, schema refs)
- signed_manifest.sig (optional, request if you require PGP verification)
- sha256sum.txt (human-readable list)
- exportpackage.tar.gz (or folder of objects for S3 delivery)
- redaction_rules.yaml (if redacted)
- delivery_proof.txt (URLs, expiry, and transfer logs)

If you confirm the window I'll kick this off.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Audit & Compliance Operations — Redwood Inference

On a related note: Internal note to team — if HelixCare requests the customer-specific salt for tokenization we must escalate and route through Legal (we do not provide salts).
